documents.title: Press Release - CPCL Financial Performance For The Quarter And Half Year Ended 30.09.2026
Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Press Release / Media Release
Audited Financial Results For The Quarter And Half Year Ended 30.09.2026

analysis.summary: Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited reported its financial and operational performance for Q4 and FY25-26, highlighting record-high crude throughput, distillate yield, and value-added product output. Management noted robust operational metrics despite geopolitical headwinds and logistical disruptions affecting crude sourcing, particularly from the Middle East. The board recommended a final dividend of INR54 per share, taking total dividends for the year to INR62 per share. Looking ahead, the company is advancing its Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS and retail outlet projects while maintaining disciplined capital allocation and comfortable leverage levels. Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited (CPCL) reported its financial and operational performance for the fourth quarter and full year of FY 2024-25, highlighting resilient operational metrics, capacity utilization, and energy efficiency improvements despite lower international product cracks affecting overall profitability.

demand_outlook.claim: The management noted that the southern market exhibits a clear shortfall in Motor Spirit (MS), where production is less than demand.
demand_outlook.quote: MS in southern market, there is a clear shortfall so, the production is less than demand.

demand_outlook.claim: Management stated that MS demand in the southern market is projected to grow around 4% to 5%.
demand_outlook.quote: Like MS, they are projecting 6% and here we see around 4%-5%.

demand_outlook.claim: Management noted a growth forecast of 3% for HSD in the southern market.
demand_outlook.quote: HSD we see at 3% growth forecast, as against 2.5% odd here.

capex_expansion.claim: The company has all approvals in place for the Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS project, and execution has started in full swing.
capex_expansion.quote: Some of the important projects that we'll be taking up is Group 2, Group 3 LOBS for which all approvals are in place and the project execution has started in full swing.

capex_expansion.claim: The retail outlet endeavor has taken 300 licenses and will see a lot of commissioning during the year.
capex_expansion.quote: Even our retail outlet endeavor for which we had taken 300 licenses has started. And this year, that is '26-'27, we'll see a lot of commissioning out of them.

capex_expansion.claim: The LOBS project is budgeted at INR1,600 crores and the retail outlet project at INR400 crores, totaling INR2,000 crores to be spent over 2 to 3 years.
capex_expansion.quote: LOBS project, Group 2, Group 3 LOBS project is INR1,600 crores. The retail outlet project is INR400 crores. So that makes it INR2,000 crores. This INR2,000 crores will happen over 2 to 3 years.

capex_expansion.claim: Normal annual maintenance capex is estimated at around INR500 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: Besides, every year, you can assume another INR500 crores is our normal capex.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL incurred a total capex of Rs. 673 crores for the current financial year.
capex_expansion.quote: On the CAPEX front, in the current year, we have spent Rs. 673 crores as CAPEX for the current year.

capex_expansion.claim: The revised capital cost for the Cauvery Basin Refinery project stands at Rs. 36,354 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: The revised capital cost is at Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian oil respectively.

capex_expansion.claim: Management stated that the new CBR refinery will have a capacity of 9 million metric tons and a polypropylene petrochemical intensity of 6%.
capex_expansion.quote: The new refinery capital cost is Rs 36,000 Crore approximately, 9 million metric ton capacity and petrochemical intensity of 6% and which is PP, polypropylene.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL installed a 1.04 MW capacity ground-mounted and rooftop solar power system on plant area buildings.
capex_expansion.quote: 1.04 MW capacity of Ground Mounted and Roof top solar system on plant area buildings

margins_costs.claim: The gross refining margin for quarter 4 was $13.75 per barrel compared to the Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for quarter 4 was $13.75 barrel as compared to Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel, which again reiterates that all these efficiencies are constant, continuous and are being sustained over each period.

margins_costs.claim: The core GRM for the fourth quarter was reported at $10.3 per barrel.
Foreign exchange loss was approximately INR200 crores for the quarter and around INR350 crores for the full year.
margins_costs.quote: For the quarter, it would be for the quarter, it is approximately INR 200 crores,. And for the whole year, it will be around INR350 crores.

margins_costs.claim: The full year GRM for 2024-25 was $4.22 per barrel compared to $8.64 per barrel in the previous year.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for 2024-25 for a full year basis is $4.22 per barrel as compared to the previous year $8.64 per barrel, but if you compare it to Singapore benchmark which was $3.79 per barrel in the current year, we have performed better.

margins_costs.claim: Inventory gain for the fourth quarter was $0.66 per barrel, amounting to Rs. 125 crores.
margins_costs.quote: Yes, the inventory gain is not very significant for the quarter. It is only $ 0.66 per barrel. And in absolute rupee terms, it is Rs. 125 crores only.

margins_costs.claim: Inventory on an overall annual basis registered a loss of $0.06 per barrel, translating to Rs. 40 crores.
margins_costs.quote: But on an overall annual basis, the inventory would be a loss that is $ 0.06 per barrel, Rs. 40 crores in amount.

margins_costs.claim: The fourth quarter GRM was reported at $6.22 per barrel.
margins_costs.quote: On Quarter 4, our GRM was $6.22 per barrel.

margins_costs.claim: CPCL reported a Gross Refining Margin of $3.40 per barrel for 9M FY2024-25 compared to $8.64 per barrel in FY2023-24.
Net operating expenditure was 945 crore rupees for 9M FY2024-25.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved its highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 million metric tons, equivalent to 112% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, million metric ton, which equivalents to 112% of installed capacity, breaking records of our previous best of 11.64 MMT achieved in financial year 2023-'24.

orders_capacity.claim: Crude throughput in quarter 4 reached 2.93 MMT, which is 111% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: In quarter 4 of the current financial year, CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT, which is also 111% of installed capacity.

orders_capacity.claim: The company achieved the best fuel and loss of 7.73%, MBN of 69.8%, and EII of 84% in the current financial year.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved the best fuel and loss of 7.73%, best MBN of 69.8% and best EII of 84% in the current financial year '25-'26, surpassing our previous best records achieved in the last financial year

orders_capacity.claim: Production reached highest ever levels of 5.139 MMT for diesel and 1.318 MMT for petrol, alongside a distillate yield of 79.1%.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL concluded the financial year on a high note, achieving the highest ever production levels of 5.139 MMT for diesel HSD, and 1.318 MMT of petrol that is MS, an impressive testament of the refinery's outstanding operational performance. Further, highest ever distillate yield of 79.1%, beating our previous record of 77.6% set in 2019-'20 was also achieved during this year.

orders_capacity.claim: Annual LPG production reached a record 447 TMT.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved highest ever LPG production of 447 TMT, overcoming previous record of 404 set in 2023-'24.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT, representing 99.5% of installed capacity during the year.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT, equivalent to 99.5% of our installed capacity and this must be seen with respect to the turnaround that has happened during the year

orders_capacity.claim: Crude throughput for Quarter 4 was 2.974 MMT, reaching 113% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: and coming on to Quarter 4, the crude throughput was 2.974, which is 113% of installed capacity.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL's Manali Refinery has a capacity of 10.5 MMTPA.

capital_allocation.claim: The leverage position stands at 0.18 on a gross debt-to-equity level.
capital_allocation.quote: Our leverage position now stands at 0.18. Our debt equity stands at 0.18 at a gross level as compared to 0.39 last year.

capital_allocation.claim: Gross borrowings stand at INR1,900 crores, while net borrowings are INR973 crores with a net debt ratio of 0.09.
capital_allocation.quote: On a gross basis, the borrowings are INR1,900 crores, but on a net basis, it is less than INR1,000 crores, to be precise, INR973 crores. If we consider net borrowing, the debt ratio is only 0.09, which is less than 0.1.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board recommended a final dividend of INR54 per share, bringing the total dividend for the year to INR62 per share inclusive of the interim dividend of INR8.
capital_allocation.quote: During the year, for the first time, CPCL paid an interim dividend, and we are happy to announce that in addition to the interim dividend of INR8 per equity share of INR10 each, the Board has recommended a final dividend of INR54 per share, taking the total dividend for the year to INR62 per share, which again is highest ever.

capital_allocation.claim: Capex incurred during the current year was INR856 crores compared to INR673 crores in the previous year.
capital_allocation.quote: During the current year, the capex was INR856 crores as compared to INR673 crores in the previous year.

capital_allocation.claim: The debt-equity ratio as of March 31, 2025, stood at 0.39 compared to 0.32 in the previous year.
capital_allocation.quote: When I turn to leverage position, the debt equity position as on March 31, 2025, is 0.39 compared to 0.32 in the previous year.

capital_allocation.claim: Total debt at an absolute level stood at Rs. 3,100 crores as of March 31, 2025.
capital_allocation.quote: At an absolute level, the debt stands at Rs. 3,100 crores as compared to Rs. 2,762 crores as on March 31, 2024.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share, representing 50% of the face value.
capital_allocation.quote: With the above, the Board has also recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share that is 50% of face value for the current year and as we all know, this is subject to approval at AGM, which will happen in the due course.

capital_allocation.claim: CPCL's net worth stood at 7491 crore rupees as of December 2024.

risks_headwinds.claim: Uncertainties due to logistical constraints and volatility of crude oil prices pose challenges.
risks_headwinds.quote: Now with all this, I would like to say the uncertainties due to logistical constraints, volatility of crude oil prices do pose challenges.

risks_headwinds.claim: Management noted that uncertainties due to the volatility of crude prices pose a challenge.
risks_headwinds.quote: Finally, the uncertainties due to volatility of crude prices do pose a challenge.

risks_headwinds.claim: CPCL recorded an exchange variation loss of 122 crore rupees in 9M FY2024-25.
CPCL provided 9 crore rupees for contingent liabilities during 9M FY2024-25.

management_commitments.claim: Management stated that the Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS and retail outlet projects will involve an outlay of INR2,000 crores over 2 to 3 years.
management_commitments.quote: This INR2,000 crores will happen over 2 to 3 years.

management_commitments.claim: Maintenance capex is expected to remain in the range of Rs. 200 to Rs. 250 crores.
management_commitments.quote: Our maintenance CAPEX remains Rs. 200-250 crore range, and the next year forecast also, we feel the CAPEX will be in that range.

management_commitments.claim: Normal maintenance capex for the next two years is projected around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores per year.
management_commitments.quote: The normal maintenance CAPEX for the next two years would be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores, maintenance CAPEX plus small regular CAPEX normally.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
